chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad and Yahya ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

We were with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), about thirty men, when my father entered. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) welcomed him and seated him by his side, then faced him for a long time. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Muawiya has a need, so if you would lighten [the gathering], we will all stand up.' So my father said to me: 'Return, O Muawiya!' So I returned.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is your son?' He said: 'Yes, and he alleges that the people of Medina are doing something that is not permissible for them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is it?' I said: 'The Qurashi Hashimite woman rides [a slave] and places her hand on the head of the black [slave], and her forearms on his neck.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son, do you not read the Quran?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Recite this verse: There is no blame on them [the wives] in respect of their fathers, nor their sons, until he reached: nor of what their right hands possess.'
Then he said: 'O my son, there is no problem if the slave sees the hair and the leg.'

key_terms.الْقُرَشِيَّةَ: The woman from the Quraysh tribe
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكُ: The slave (male or female, contextually male here)
key_terms.الْهَاشِمِيَّةَ: The woman from the Hashim clan
key_terms.لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ: There is no blame on them

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on a mistress looking at her slave's body parts according to Hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of a mistress looking at her slave's hair and legs, citing the Quranic verse (Surah al-Ahzab, 33:55) which lists those whom wives may look at without blame, including 'what their right hands possess.' The narration uses the example of a noble Qurashi woman riding a black slave to illustrate this ruling. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for defining the limits of visual modesty (awrah) for slaves, distinguishing between the general public gaze and the specific permissions granted within the household context.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad and Yahya Bin Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is it?’ I said, ‘The Qureyshi Hashimite woman rode and placed her hand upon the head of the black (slave), and her arm was upon his neck’.

So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘O myasws son! Have you not read the Quran?’ I said, ‘Yes’. Heasws said: ‘Recite this Verse [33:55] There is no blame on them (wives) in respect of their fathers, nor their sons’ until heasws reached ‘nor of what their right hands possess’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> son! There is no problem if the slave were to see the hair and the leg’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Ibrahim ibn abu al-Balad and Yahya ibn Ibrahim from his father Ibrahim from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“Once we, about thirty people, were with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when my father came and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, welcomed him, gave him a place just next to himself and turned to him (for speaking) for a long time. Then abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Abu Mu‘awiyah needs privacy, if you please provide us relief.’ We all got up and my father said to me, ‘O Mu‘awiyah, come back.’

I turned back and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, asked, ‘Is this your son?’ He replied, ‘Yes, and he thinks that people of al-Madinah do something unlawful.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What is it?’ I then said, ‘The woman of Quraysh or of Banu Hashim when riding, places her hand on the head of the black (slave) and her arms on his neck.’

Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Son, have you not read al-Quran?’ I replied, ‘Yes, I read it.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Read this verse, ‘. . . it is not unlawful for them about their fathers, sons, and whomever their right hands possess.’ [33:55]
He (the Imam) then said, ‘It is not unlawful if a slave looks at one’s hairs and legs (below the knees).”’
